import pandas as pd

# File paths for all source CSV files
source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_34/test_0.csv"
source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_34/test_1.csv"
source2_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_34/test_2.csv"
source3_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_34/test_3.csv"
source4_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_34/test_4.csv"

# Load all source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the first numerical index column
df0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path, index_col=0)  # ['batsman', 'batsman_runs']
df1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path, index_col=0)  # ['batsman', 'total_runs']
df2 = pd.read_csv(source2_path, index_col=0)  # ['batsman', 'no of balls', 'batsman_runs', 'strike']
df3 = pd.read_csv(source3_path, index_col=0)  # ['batsman', 'batsman_runs']
df4 = pd.read_csv(source4_path, index_col=0)  # ['batsman', 'total_runs']

# --- Transformation Plan ---
# Target schema:
# ['batsman': string,
#  'total_runs_x': integer,
#  'batsman_runs_x': integer,
#  'batsman_runs_y': integer,
#  'no of balls': integer,
#  'batsman_runs': integer,
#  'strike': float,
#  'total_runs_y': integer]

# Observations:
# - batsman is the join key for all tables.
# - total_runs_x and total_runs_y come from two different sources with total_runs column:
#   df1 and df4 both have ['batsman', 'total_runs'].
#   We will rename df1.total_runs -> total_runs_x
#   and df4.total_runs -> total_runs_y
# - batsman_runs_x and batsman_runs_y come from two different sources with batsman_runs column:
#   df0 and df3 both have ['batsman', 'batsman_runs'].
#   We will rename df0.batsman_runs -> batsman_runs_x
#   and df3.batsman_runs -> batsman_runs_y
# - df2 has ['batsman', 'no of balls', 'batsman_runs', 'strike']
#   The 'batsman_runs' here corresponds to the target column 'batsman_runs' (without suffix)
#   'no of balls' and 'strike' also come from df2.
# - All sources have 516 or 258 rows, but the target has 258 rows, which matches df1 (258 rows).
#   So df1 is the base table to join others on batsman.
# - Join order:
#   Start from df1 (total_runs_x)
#   Join df4 (total_runs_y) on batsman
#   Join df0 (batsman_runs_x) on batsman
#   Join df3 (batsman_runs_y) on batsman
#   Join df2 (no of balls, batsman_runs, strike) on batsman
# - After joining, select and reorder columns as per target schema.
# - Convert data types to match target schema:
#   total_runs_x, batsman_runs_x, batsman_runs_y, no of balls, batsman_runs, total_runs_y -> int
#   strike -> float
#   batsman -> string (already string)
# - Handle missing values if any by filling with 0 or appropriate default (since target examples have no missing).

# Rename columns to avoid collision before join
df1_renamed = df1.rename(columns={"total_runs": "total_runs_x"})
df4_renamed = df4.rename(columns={"total_runs": "total_runs_y"})
df0_renamed = df0.rename(columns={"batsman_runs": "batsman_runs_x"})
df3_renamed = df3.rename(columns={"batsman_runs": "batsman_runs_y"})

# Merge step by step on 'batsman'
df_merge = df1_renamed.merge(df4_renamed, on="batsman", how="inner")
df_merge = df_merge.merge(df0_renamed, on="batsman", how="inner")
df_merge = df_merge.merge(df3_renamed, on="batsman", how="inner")
df_merge = df_merge.merge(df2, on="batsman", how="inner")

# Select and reorder columns as per target schema
target_columns = [
    "batsman",
    "total_runs_x",
    "batsman_runs_x",
    "batsman_runs_y",
    "no of balls",
    "batsman_runs",
    "strike",
    "total_runs_y",
]

df_target = df_merge[target_columns]

# Convert data types to match target schema
df_target["total_runs_x"] = df_target["total_runs_x"].astype(int)
df_target["batsman_runs_x"] = df_target["batsman_runs_x"].astype(int)
df_target["batsman_runs_y"] = df_target["batsman_runs_y"].astype(int)
df_target["no of balls"] = df_target["no of balls"].astype(int)
df_target["batsman_runs"] = df_target["batsman_runs"].astype(int)
df_target["strike"] = df_target["strike"].astype(float)
df_target["total_runs_y"] = df_target["total_runs_y"].astype(int)

# Write the result to the specified output path
output_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_34/target_multisource_cot.csv"
df_target.to_csv(output_path, index=False)
